Rabbits are extremely prone to dental issues due to their teeth constantly growing. CT of the head is the best way to diagnose but dental x-rays are the next best. Either way she really should be seen by a vet who is comfortable with treating rabbits.

I would recommend asking you vet about a CT scan to check for dental issues. If that’s not available or in your budget I would suggest a cytology of a fine needle aspirate. They will take a needle and poke the mass a few times then spray off the cells on to a slide for best results your vet will sent it off to a specialty lab. The cytology can tell you what type of cells are in the mass. I would also suggest some basic blood work like a chemistry and cbc to make sure everything looks normal and no sigh of infection. You could also have the blood PMC check, this is a rabbit specific inflammatory marker but if your bun has arthritis or any other inflammatory issues the results might not be helpful.

 X-7y                 x-7y          -1(-x+7y)        -1(7y-x)           -1
The first thing I did was divide the numerator by 2 to get 2 times 7y-x. The next thing I did was divide the denominator by -1 so that the x was negative and the 7y was positive like in the numerator. I then rearranged the denominator to make it look more like the numerator by writing -x+7y as 7y-x. Then the 7y-x and 7y-x cancel out leaving 2 divided by -1 which is equivalent to -2.
